newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rail workers stage national strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rail workers stage national strike.

text.p: Some 14,000 workers from Croatia's state railways (HZ) went on strike on Thursday, but the government said it was standing firm and was not ready to negotiate their demands, state news agency Hina reported.
The strikers have vowed to keep rail traffic at a standstill until their demands for a wage increase and safer working conditions are met.
However, two out of three railway trade unions backed out after talks with traffic minister Zeljko Luzavec.
"This is an unnecessary strike. The reasons for it are quite different from those the workers stated," said Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa after a cabinet session.

HINA said most traffic in the snow-swept country, save for international and cargo trains, ground to a halt at 1000 local (0900 GMT). Strikers said some 20 percent of passenger trains continued to roll.

Luzavec said salaries of Croatian Railways (HZ) employees had gone up 21 percent this year. The government has thus met all obligations from the collective agreements it earlier reached with HZ, he said.
Croatian parliament is due to discuss the rehabilitation and restructuring of the loss-making railway company soon.
The rail strike follows a wave of protests in Croatia in the past week as pensioners, teachers and public sector workers have taken to the streets to demand pay and pension increases.
Living standards in the former Yugoslav republic have plunged since 1993, when the government launched a harsh stabilisation programme to curb hyperinflation.
